invariants.INV-01: A retry of the same logical write reuses the same event_id.
invariants.INV-02: Same idempotency key and same payload digest yields duplicate with no second effect.
invariants.INV-03: Same idempotency key with a different payload is rejected and nothing is written.
invariants.INV-04: ACK is returned only after the PostgreSQL transaction is committed; process-crash durable, not host-loss durable.
invariants.INV-05: A connection lost after commit is unknown_commit_status, resolved by receipt lookup or identical retry.
invariants.INV-06: CAS on expected_revision prevents lost updates.
invariants.INV-07: A lower revision never moves state backwards.
invariants.INV-08: Conflicts are surfaced, never silently resolved last-write-wins.
invariants.INV-09: A checkpoint is always a new event; no prior checkpoint is updated or deleted.
invariants.INV-10: A candidate becomes a fact only through an authorised promotion naming principal and evidence.
invariants.INV-11: Multi-valued facts never auto-supersede each other.
invariants.INV-12: A tombstone survives projection rebuild and backup restore.
invariants.INV-13: ACL is applied before retrieval and before any embedding or LLM egress.
invariants.INV-14: Secret/PII-shaped content is rejected before persistence, commit and egress; payload is never logged.
invariants.INV-15: Recalled text is data, never instruction or authorization.
invariants.INV-16: A subagent may submit evidence but cannot mutate the parent work's active state.
invariants.INV-17: A client-declared scope is intersected with the granted scope; it can never widen it.
invariants.INV-18: After fencing, an older writer epoch is rejected.
invariants.INV-19: A branch rewind creates lineage; it deletes no events.
invariants.INV-20: Canonical ordering is events.seq; client clocks never decide order.
